prompt: A database volume snapshot is Ready, but isolated restore fails application consistency. Lead response and prevention.
directAnswer: Declare data/RPO impact, preserve source PVC/PV/snapshot/content UIDs, handles, transaction/checkpoint/WAL positions and timing. Ready proves infrastructure snapshot completion only. Keep original read-only/protected, restore to a new claim, run storage integrity and application-native recovery. Determine whether quiesce/checkpoint/log shipping was absent or ordering violated. Recover through database procedures, verify business transactions and user operation, record actual RPO/RTO, retain evidence, and redesign scheduled application-consistent backup plus recurring restore drills.
foundation: Snapshot completion and application-consistent recoverability are different claims.
seniorAnswer: I reject the green-snapshot fallacy, preserve the source and perform isolated application-aware recovery. Closure is correct business state and user behavior, not mounted files.
weakAnswer: Take another snapshot and overwrite the original restore.
whyWeak: It can destroy evidence and repeats an unproven consistency process.

followUps.answer: Crash-consistent captures storage point; app-consistent coordinates application state.
Protects the only source and permits verification.
Backup age/success plus scheduled restore RPO/RTO and integrity.
